test_title: SSC GD Constable (2022) Official Paper (Held On : 27 Jan 2023 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Radius of a sphere is 6 cm. The numerical value of the surface area of this sphere is what percentage of the numerical value of its volume?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The numerical ratio of Surface Area to Volume of any sphere is always 3/r.

Required Percentage = (3 ÷ r) × 100

Substitute the given radius r = 6 cm:

Required Percentage = (3 ÷ 6) × 100 = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b4beee7d06e800082e2269dfbeb8efa08455e15b3b7f86f11a27b3f25638a021.png] 

**Given:**

⇒ Radius of the sphere (r) = 6 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Surface Area of a sphere = 4 × π × r²

⇒ Volume of a sphere = 4/3 × π × r³

**Calculation:**

⇒ Surface Area = 4 × π × (6)²

⇒ Surface Area = 144π cm²

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × (6)³

⇒ Volume = 4/3 × π × 216

⇒ Volume = 288π cm³

⇒ Required Percentage = (Surface Area ÷ Volume) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (144π ÷ 288π) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = (1 ÷ 2) × 100

⇒ Required Percentage = 50%

**∴ The correct answer is 50%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Hemisphere Formulas

The volume of a hemisphere is 2/3 × πr³. Its Curved Surface Area (CSA) is 2πr², and Total Surface Area (TSA) is 3πr².

Surface Area to Volume Ratio

The ratio of the surface area to the volume for a sphere mathematically simplifies to 3 ÷ r. This indicates that as the radius increases, the volume capacity grows significantly faster than its outer surface area.

Total vs Curved Surface Area

For a complete sphere, the Total Surface Area and Curved Surface Area are exactly identical (4πr²) because the continuous shape does not contain any flat base section.
